title: Optimize walkthrough: quantization profiles INT8/FP8 - quality vs latency
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles, demonstrating quality vs latency comparisons using customer-like workloads. Discussion covered profiling approach, expected accuracy drift, fallback policies, and pilot steps (benchmark run, security docs, pricing). Customer expressed interest in a 2-week pilot and asked for SLA/throughput targets and security artifacts.

transcript:
[00:00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): All right good afternoon everyone uh thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out the time. quick around the room?
[00:00:10] Alex (Nimble CTO): Alex here, Priya, Jordan and Sam on our side.
[00:00:14] Priya (ML Eng): Hi Priya, thanks for doing this.
[00:00:16] Samantha (Product): Sam here.
[00:00:18] Maya (Redwood SE): Maya from Redwood, hi everyone, I'll drive the Optimize walkthrough and show the INT8 and FP8 profiles, plus quality vs latency charts.
[00:00:27] Ethan: Quick agenda: walkthrough, benchmarking methodology, demo of the console + live perf numbers, then pilot scope and next steps. sound good?
[00:00:33] Alex: Yep sounds great.
[00:00:36] Maya: Cool, jumping in. So first, for context, Optimize is our toolkit that recommends batching, cache, and quantization profiles per-model and per-workload. today we'll focus on quantization: INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs.
[00:00:48] Maya: [00:00:48] (slides) We typically profile for three buckets: throughput-heavy online inference, latency-sensitive interactive, and mixed. quantization profiles depend on sequence length, token distribution, and model family.
[00:01:02] Priya: Quick question: for our use case, most queries are < 150 tokens but we have long-context retrieval occasionally up to 1k. which profile should we expect?
[00:01:10] Maya: Good point, you'd get a hybrid recommendation. INT8 often gives best cost and good throughput but sometimes shows slight quality degradation on long-contexts; FP8 hits a middle ground, lower memory and latency than FP16 but often better quality than naive INT8.
[00:01:24] Jordan (Infra): Are these quantized models compatible with Dedicated pools? we need to lock down capacity.
[00:01:30] Luis (Redwood): yes Dedicated/Dedicated pools and Private installs both supported. the runtime will select kernels accordingly; on some hw FP8 paths need newer drivers but we manage that in Dedicated.
[00:01:39] Maya: moving to the demo, here's the console: per-model quant profiles, and a quality vs latency scatter chart.
[00:01:46] Maya: [00:01:46] (typing sounds) okay pulling up the benchmark for model-x-13b. we ran benchmarks with your sample prompts (synthetic paraphrases of retail checkout flows).
[00:01:58] Maya: [00:01:58] baseline is fp16, then int8, then fp8 quant. latency numbers are p50/p95 and tokens/sec.
[00:02:08] Ethan: Note: transcription may mangle some words but the gist is the charts.
[00:02:12] Maya: on these prompts int8 reduces token compute by ~2.6x and latency p95 improved from 420ms to 160ms on our Dedicated 4xA100-like setup, but we saw a small BLEU/perplexity-like delta that in some instruction-following prompts caused occasional truncation or subtle style differences.
[00:02:29] Priya: how big was the quality delta? could you point to an example?
[00:02:34] Maya: yeah for our retail QA examples, average exact-match dropped from 92% to 90% and for freer text instructions we saw some hallucination rate go from 3% to 5% on int8; fp8 kept it at ~92/3.5% so FP8 was a good compromise.
[00:02:49] Alex: ok that seems acceptable if we can monitor and roll back per-route.
[00:02:54] Maya: exactly -- Optimize can recommend profiles and we link to rollouts where you can canary a profile on X% of traffic, and automatic rollback if eval metrics cross thresholds.
[00:03:03] Samantha: how do we define the eval metrics? can we plug in our own eval set?
[00:03:07] Maya: yes you upload a labeled prompt set to Optimize, and we run the same prompts across profiles and compute your chosen metrics (exact-match, f1, perplexity, custom classifiers).
[00:03:17] Ethan: also we maintain KV/prefix cache metrics; for short queries caching can make quantization less impactful because you hit cached KV more often.
[00:03:26] [00:03:26] (brief ambient noise)
[00:03:30] Maya: moving to latency SLOs: we provide latency budgeting per-route; Optimize suggests batch sizes, micro-batching, and quant profiles to meet p95 targets. For your target of 200ms p95, FP8 looked like the safe pick for mixed workloads.
[00:03:45] Jordan: 200ms p95 is our internal goal. if int8 gets to 160ms p95 should we pick int8?
[00:03:51] Maya: it's tradeoff -- int8 could hit latency and cost targets but risk small quality regressions. we recommend pilot testing with a 10-20% traffic canary.
[00:03:59] Priya: regarding model variants and fallback -- if int8 fails the quality test at runtime do you automatically route to fp16?
[00:04:05] Maya: you can configure fallback policies: on inference-time confidence below threshold we route to a higher-precision variant (fp8 or fp16). these add tail latency and cost for those requests but keep overall user experience intact.
[00:04:16] Ethan: quick note on measurement: we compute per-token latency excluding networking where possible, and provide server-side p50/p95 plus end-to-end numbers from SDK.
[00:04:26] Alex: nice. can you share the raw benchmark CSVs?
[00:04:29] Maya: yes we'll share the CSV and our Jupyter notebook that replays prompts and computes metrics (link posted after).
[00:04:35] Maya: [00:04:35] (typo) I just pulled the int8 artifact and there's a sample where the reply loses a line -- that's the kind of regression we flagged.
[00:04:44] Priya: This is important: our compliance team will want to see audit logs when fallback happens. do you log model variant and decision triggers?
[00:04:51] Luis: yes we emit trace events with model_version, quant_profile, decision_reason and a request_id for correlation; available in Console traces and to our SIEM via audit export.
[00:05:00] Jordan: and encryption? we need KMS and HSM key policies for Private deployment.
[00:05:04] Luis: supported -- HSM integration and customer-managed KMS in Private; Dedicated supports KMS with key rotation. we'll include integration notes.
[00:05:10] Samantha: what's the expected reduction in cost with int8 vs fp16?
[00:05:14] Maya: depends on throughput, but on average int8 reduced token compute cost ~40-55% vs fp16; FP8 was ~20-35% cost reduction with better quality retention.
[00:05:24] Alex: can we run these on our on-prem, or do we need Dedicated?
[00:05:27] Ethan: Private on-prem is possible -- we'll work with your infra team on driver/toolchain compatibility. fp8 paths sometimes require vendor drivers for optimal kernels.
[00:05:36] [00:05:36] (speaker coughs)
[00:05:38] Maya: demoing the console's Optimize tab: here you can see per-route suggestions, recommended profile, expected latency delta, and confidence band. you can click to run a local simulation using your eval set in the browser (we stream a job).
[00:05:54] Priya: Is the simulation deterministic? we need reproducible comparisons.
[00:05:57] Maya: we seed RNG and capture tokenization differences; results are reproducible given the same model snapshot and quant artifact.
[00:06:06] Ethan: ok switching to a slightly deeper technical slide -- how we build int8: we quantize weight matrices with outlier handling, per-channel calibration; for FP8 we use shared exponent strategies that preserve dynamic range for attention logits.
[00:06:21] Maya: listeners may hear some jargon but the upshot is FP8 keeps precision where it's needed while still saving memory and compute.
[00:06:29] Alex: are there any known failure modes? like repeated hallucinations?
[00:06:32] Maya: yes edge cases: chain-of-thought or very long context summarization sometimes suffers under aggressive int8. we recommend measuring your critical prompts first.
[00:06:42] Jordan: what's the time to produce a quantized artifact?
[00:06:45] Maya: artifact build time depends on model size and node type; typical 13B model takes 20-40 minutes in our pipeline, with profiling steps. we cache artifacts per model+config.
[00:06:55] Priya: do you support mixed precision (pfp16 + int8) per-layer?
[00:06:59] Maya: yes hybrid strategies are supported -- some layers stay fp16 while others quantized; Optimize can suggest layer-level mixes if required.
[00:07:07] Ethan: moving to pilot discussion: suggested scope is 2 weeks, run your 5k-10k prompt eval set across fp16, fp8, int8, measure exact-match/f1 and p95 latency, run canary at 10% traffic.
[00:07:19] Samantha: budget?
[00:07:21] Ethan: we'll send a pilot pricing sheet; typical pilot costs are partial Dedicated credits plus engineering time -- we'll include an estimate for a 2-week run.
[00:07:30] Priya: can we get SSO and RBAC configured for our team?
[00:07:33] Luis: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM user sync, and RBAC are supported; we'll include setup steps.
[00:07:40] [00:07:40] (keystrokes)
[00:08:02] Maya: showing a live replay of sample prompt A -- fp16 answer vs int8 answer; you can see int8 omits a clarification sentence.
[00:08:12] Priya: hmm that could impact UX in checkout. we need to make sure any regressions are tolerable.
[00:08:17] Maya: agreed which is why we recommend canary + monitoring + rollback.
[00:08:21] Alex: will you provide hooks to our monitoring stack for custom alerts?
[00:08:25] Luis: yes we stream metrics (latency, token counts, quant_profile usage) to your metrics backend and can emit alerts for metric deltas.
[00:08:33] Maya: we also show a per-prompt diff UI so you can review failing prompts and classify them to improve fit.
[00:08:40] [00:08:40] (background voice)
[00:08:44] Ethan: any other technical deep dives you want to do today?
[00:08:46] Priya: Could we run a short profiling session with our prompts during the pilot?
[00:08:50] Maya: absolutely; we'll provide scripts that replay prompts at realistic QPS and capture detailed traces.
[00:08:57] Alex: timeline -- if we kick off next week when can we expect results?
[00:09:01] Maya: two-week pilot; first week profiling and artifact builds, second week canary and production-like run; we'll share interim results by end of week 1.
[00:09:09] Samantha: for procurement/compliance we need the SOC2 doc and a copy of the contract.
[00:09:14] Ethan: will send both -- Luis will attach SOC2 and KMS notes.
[00:09:19] [00:09:19] (typing)
[00:09:25] Priya: anything else on metrics? what about cost attribution per feature?
[00:09:29] Ethan: Console gives token-level cost and per-route breakdown, you can map requests to product features.
[00:09:35] Maya: and Optimize can simulate cost-savings per profile so you can see monetary impact of switching to FP8 vs INT8.
[00:09:43] Jordan: for Dedicated sizing do you have guidance? our peak is about 380 concurrent sessions.
[00:09:49] Luis: we'll map QPS and seq length distribution to GPU counts; export a sizing spreadsheet after we get your sample logs.
[00:09:56] Alex: ok let's confirm folks for pilot: Ethan, Maya, Luis from Redwood; Priya and Jordan on our side. Sam will handle product acceptance.
[00:10:04] Ethan: great, I'll send meeting notes and pilot contract. Maya will upload notebooks and scripts.
[00:10:09] Maya: quick clarifying Q -- Priya, can you share the typical prompt breakdown (percent short vs long) in a spreadsheet?
[00:10:15] Priya: yes I'll share that today.
[00:10:18] [00:10:18] (brief pause)
[00:10:22] Ethan: wrap-up: explicit next steps -- pilot proposal, scripts, SOC2, schedule follow-up. thanks everyone.
[00:10:29] Alex: thanks all.
[00:10:32] Samantha: thank you.
[00:10:34] [00:10:34] (call ends)
